name: Porro-prism binoculars
definition: twin-barrel binoculars with Porro prisms, giving an offset, Z-shaped body.
notes: Porro prisms are a Bauart filter in a 232-product shop category

name: Giant binoculars
definition: binoculars of 70 to 150 mm aperture, used on a tripod.
notes: Shop lists 70-100 mm and 40x150 Porro binoculars as astronomy models; Wikipedia gives 70-150 mm

name: Opera glasses
definition: small Galilean-design binoculars for the theatre and opera.
notes: Page calls opera glasses Galilean binoculars with central focus; lorgnette and chain types

name: Monocular
definition: single-tube handheld viewing instrument, not a telescope on a mount.
notes: Monoculars sold as their own product type beside binoculars

name: Night-vision viewer
definition: viewer that intensifies available light to show a scene in the dark (rule T(b), C6-O1: provisional until attested).
notes: Night-vision monoculars (PVS-14) and goggles sold under one night-vision shop

name: Thermal-imaging viewer
definition: viewer that shows a scene by the heat it gives off (rule T(b), C6-O1: provisional until attested).
notes: Thermal imaging monoculars sold as a product range

name: Roof-prism binoculars
definition: twin-barrel binoculars with roof prisms, giving a straight, slim body.
notes: Product page gives type of build Roof with phase-correction coated roof prisms

name: Refractor telescope
definition: telescope that gathers light with a lens objective.
notes: Refractor category with achromat and apochromat (doublet, triplet) tubes

name: Newtonian reflector telescope
definition: telescope that gathers light with a primary mirror and a flat secondary mirror at the side of the tube; the Dobsonian is a named form of it, not a kind (C-18).
notes: Newton is a type-of-build filter (340 products); Dobsonians sold within it

name: Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope
definition: catadioptric telescope with a corrector plate and a folded mirror light path.
notes: Schmidt-Cassegrain is a type-of-build filter (37); EdgeHD and ACF variants listed separately

name: Maksutov-Cassegrain telescope
definition: catadioptric telescope with a meniscus corrector and a folded mirror light path.
notes: Maksutov-Cassegrain is a catadioptric category with OTAs and mounted sets

name: Smart (imaging) telescope
definition: telescope with a sensor and no eyepiece that shows the sky on a screen or app (rule T(b), C6-O1: provisional until attested).
notes: Smart Telescopes is a type-of-build filter (32) and a shop category

name: Solar (H-alpha) telescope
definition: telescope made to observe the Sun in hydrogen-alpha light (rule T(b), C6-O1: provisional until attested).
notes: Solar telescopes category with H-Alpha build type (34 of 37) from Lunt, DayStar, Sky-Watcher

name: Spotting scope
definition: compact single-tube telescope for daytime viewing of distant things, used on a tripod or rest.
notes: Spotting scopes sold as a category with angled and straight viewing; used with tripod

name: Compound light microscope
definition: microscope with an objective and an eyepiece in series, for thin specimens on a slide.
notes: Page describes compound microscope for thin specimens such as blood and bacteria; sold with Omano brand

name: Stereo (dissecting) microscope
definition: low-power microscope with two optical paths giving an upright three-dimensional view of solid objects.
notes: Stereo microscope category with Greenough and CMO optical systems, binocular and trinocular

name: Digital microscope
definition: microscope with its own sensor that shows the image on a screen or computer (rule T(b), C6-O1: provisional until attested).
notes: Digital microscope category of 132 products incl. USB hand microscopes and LCD models

name: Polarizing microscope
definition: microscope that lights the specimen with polarized light, for minerals and crystals.
notes: Polarising microscopes are a subcategory of upright microscopes, for mineralogy and petrography

name: Handheld magnifier
definition: magnifying lens on a handle held in the hand.
notes: Hand held loupe is a magnifying-glass subcategory (35 products)

name: Pocket (folding) loupe
definition: small loupe that folds into a case or holder to be carried.
notes: Folding magnifier is a subcategory (59 products), incl. Zeiss aplanatic folding magnifier

name: Stand magnifier
definition: magnifier on a desk, floor or neck-cord stand.
notes: Stand magnifiers and table-top magnifiers are subcategories (67 and 7)

name: Head-worn magnifier
definition: loupe or magnifier on a headband or clip, also called a binocular loupe (K-135, R-13).
notes: Headband Magnifiers is a subcategory (16 products); Levenhuk Zeno Vizor series

name: Eclipse viewing glasses
definition: glasses with a solar filter made for looking at the Sun (K-135).
notes: Solar eclipse glasses and viewers sold as a product group

name: Orrery
definition: mechanical model of the Sun, planets and moons (C-18).
notes: Museum holds 49 orrery objects, incl. makers of planetary models (Trippensee, W and S Jones, Space Educational Aids)

name: Astrolabe
definition: instrument that models the sky for finding the positions of stars and the time (C-18).
notes: Planispheric astrolabes sold as antiques; museum holds an electrotype copy made 1876

name: Planetarium projector
definition: projector that shows the night sky on a dome or wall (C-18).
notes: Planetaria subcategory (44) of home planetarium projectors, with discs; Sega Toys Homestar

name: Thermometer (air)
definition: instrument that reads the air temperature indoors or outdoors; a working Galileo thermometer is this kind.
notes: Galileo Thermometer and Fischer cockpit thermometer sold in the weather category

name: Hygrometer
definition: instrument that reads the humidity of the air.
notes: Fischer Hygrometer POLAR and sauna thermohygrometer sold as humidity instruments

name: Cistern barometer
definition: mercury barometer whose column stands in an open cistern.
notes: Cistern barometer in museum collection (Quare); Kew-pattern fixed-cistern mercury barometer by P Adie

name: Angle (diagonal) barometer
definition: mercury barometer whose tube is bent or sloped to lengthen the scale.
notes: Angle or diagonal barometer by Thomas Page and Angelo Lovi in museum collection

name: Aneroid barometer
definition: barometer that reads pressure from a sealed flexible capsule.
notes: Aneroid barometers sold new (Fischer precision aneroid) and as antiques

name: Wind vane
definition: instrument that shows the wind direction.
notes: Rooster weathervane with brass compass directionals sold as wind vane

name: Windsock
definition: tapered fabric sleeve that shows wind direction and strength.
notes: Airport windsock in orange polyester, FAA-compliant sizes

name: Rain gauge
definition: instrument that collects and measures rainfall.
notes: Bresser Professional rain gauge sold in weather category

name: Pyranometer
definition: instrument that measures solar radiation.
notes: Apogee SP-110 silicon pyranometer measuring total sun and sky radiation

name: Weather station
definition: instrument set that measures several weather quantities together; `sensor_suite`, `sensor_count`, `link`, `shield` and display type are attributes (C14(c)).
notes: Weather stations: wireless (28) and classic (35) subcategories; MeteoChamp 9-in-1

name: Air-quality monitor
definition: instrument that measures pollutants or particles in the air (K-147).
notes: Airthings View Plus measures radon, PM2.5, CO2, VOC; CO2 monitors in astroshop weather category

name: Anemometer
definition: instrument that measures wind speed.
notes: Handheld paddle-wheel anemometer (Extech) measuring wind speed in m/s, knots, Beaufort

name: Beaker
definition: wide cylindrical open vessel with a spout, for holding, mixing and heating liquids.
notes: Beakers listed in lab glassware category

name: Erlenmeyer flask
definition: conical flask with a narrow neck, for mixing and heating.
notes: Erlenmeyer flasks listed beside volumetric and Fernbach flasks; conical flat-bottom products

name: Volumetric flask
definition: flat-bottomed flask with a long neck and a single mark, for making a solution to an exact volume.
notes: Volumetric flasks listed in flask category

name: Round-bottom flask
definition: round flask for heating and boiling liquids.
notes: Round bottom flasks, heavy wall single and two neck

name: Test tube
definition: small tube closed at one end, for holding or heating a small sample.
notes: Culture and test tubes listed in lab glassware

name: Graduated cylinder
definition: tall cylinder with a volume scale, for measuring liquid volume.
notes: Cylinders (graduated) listed in lab glassware

name: Pipette
definition: tube for drawing up and delivering a measured amount of liquid.
notes: Pipets listed under transfer instruments; 3 ml transfer pipette in a dissecting set

name: Burette
definition: graduated tube with a tap, for delivering liquid in controlled amounts.
notes: Burettes listed under lab supplies in glassware

name: Petri dish
definition: shallow lidded dish for culturing cells or microbes.
notes: Petri and culture dishes listed in lab glassware

name: Laboratory balance
definition: balance made to weigh samples in a laboratory.
notes: Analytical and precision balances, portable balances listed

name: Centrifuge
definition: machine that spins samples to separate their parts.
notes: Benchtop, high-capacity and micro centrifuges listed

name: Laboratory incubator
definition: chamber that holds samples at a set warm temperature.
notes: Incubators: CO2, general purpose, refrigerated, shaking

name: Laboratory oven
definition: oven for drying or heating samples at a set temperature.
notes: Forced and gravity convection, vacuum, cleanroom ovens listed

name: Laboratory freezer
definition: freezer or ultra-low-temperature unit made for cold storage of samples (C-18; R-28 includes laboratory refrigerators).
notes: Laboratory freezers and refrigerators, ultra-low temperature units; Thermo Kendro TSX and Nordiclab ULT-C400

name: Fume hood
definition: ventilated cabinet that draws fumes from work on samples away from the user (C-18).
notes: Ducted and ductless fume hoods; Labconco Protector and Echo

name: Dissection set
definition: set of instruments for dissecting specimens.
notes: Dissecting set with forceps, scalpel handle, scissors, needle probes

name: Science experiment kit
definition: kit made to teach science through an experiment programme; `discipline` is an attribute (chemistry, physics and electricity, biology, earth and space, crystals and materials and others as sold) with a generated view (C-11, K-149).
notes: Kosmos Experimentierkasten sets: chemistry, physics, biology, astronomy, electronics disciplines
